newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BOK sells dollars again to cap won's fall-dealers.
newsitem.headline: BOK sells dollars again to cap won's fall-dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) intervened in the interbank foreign exchange market late Monday afternoon to boost the won against the dollar, dealers said.
The BOK was seen stepping into the market three times on Monday, they added.
The central bank intervened when the won touched 829.30, traders said. The won had fallen to a historic low of 830 to the dollar earlier in the afternoon session.
The bank stepped into the interbank market at the 823.40 and 826.60 levels in the morning session.

"Usually, the market follows the central bank's lead, with the dollar falling after the BOK steps in to support the won, but today the market has ignored the intervention," said the managing director of a local merchant bank.
The central Bank of Korea has never acknowledged that it intervenes in the market. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5644
